title: What Is a Patent Worth? Evidence from the U.S. Patent “Lottery”
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Defines the IV estimand before presenting examiner leniency; aligns first stage, instrument validity, threats, real outcomes, financing channel, and external validity.
transfer_limit: Examiner leniency and patent assignment are design-specific; do not treat a first-stage correlation or lottery metaphor as an exclusion-restriction argument.

title: Access to Collateral and the Democratization of Credit: France’s Reform of the Napoleonic Security Code
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Moves from a legal reform and treated-control construction to parallel trends, matched DiD estimates, cross-subsample checks, real effects, and bounded interpretation.
transfer_limit: Matched DiD does not eliminate unobserved differential trends, and France’s collateral codification is not a universal credit-supply shock.

title: Bad Credit, No Problem? Credit and Labor Market Consequences of Bad Credit Reports
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Links a timed reporting change to credit and labor outcomes, then separates direct outcome families and the employer-use mechanism.
transfer_limit: Timing and reporting institutions are setting-specific; employer purchases and mechanism outcomes do not automatically identify one exclusive channel.

title: Can Unemployment Insurance Spur Entrepreneurial Activity? Evidence from France
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Explains the policy comparison and identifying assumption in plain language, then distinguishes marginal effects, aggregate employment, productivity, and external validity.
transfer_limit: The treatment margin and external validity are tied to the French unemployment-insurance reform; the long concluding discussion is not a length target.

title: The Impact of Salience on Investor Behavior: Evidence from a Natural Experiment
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Turns an interface change into a natural experiment and sequences individual-level estimates, DiD confirmation, robustness, and competing behavioral mechanisms.
transfer_limit: The interface shock and brokerage population are unusual; behavioral channel evidence narrows explanations but need not prove salience uniquely.

title: The Impact of Supervision on Bank Performance
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Makes supervisory intensity, its instrument, district controls, performance outcomes, and alternative explanations separate pieces of the identification case.
transfer_limit: The supervisory-hours instrument and district structure are institutional; the result should not be generalized to all forms of supervision.

title: How Debit Cards Enable the Poor to Save More
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses an event-study DiD to establish rollout effects before survey-based evidence and a dedicated mechanism section explain why debit cards change saving.
transfer_limit: The staged rollout and account system support this event study; survey corroboration is not itself experimental mechanism identification.

title: The Impact of Repossession Risk on Mortgage Default
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Pairs a discontinuity with bandwidth checks, magnitude and external-validity discussion, and margins of excess default rather than ending at statistical significance.
transfer_limit: The discontinuity identifies a local effect and bandwidth sensitivity remains material; do not generalize it to all mortgage-default regimes.

title: The Limits of Limited Liability: Evidence from Industrial Pollution
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Connects a liability doctrine change to emissions, firm value, and solvency, and keeps the channel, heterogeneity, and robustness in distinct evidentiary blocks.
transfer_limit: Legal doctrines, environmental measurement, and corporate groups are specific; channel and heterogeneity results should not be promoted to mediation.

title: Increasing Enrollment in Income-Driven Student Loan Repayment Plans: Evidence from the Navient Field Experiment
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Separates experimental validity, intent-to-treat, local average treatment effect, borrower heterogeneity, and alternative interpretations in a field experiment.
transfer_limit: The IV/LATE interpretation depends on take-up induced by the outreach; ITT and treatment-on-treated language cannot be interchanged.

title: Borrowing to Save? The Impact of Automatic Enrollment on Debt
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Shows how an enrollment rule can answer whether induced saving changes debt, with outcomes grouped by economic margin and a concise conclusion.
transfer_limit: Automatic enrollment affects several household margins at once; reduced-form debt responses do not by themselves identify mental accounting.

title: Do Firms Respond to Gender Pay Gap Transparency?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Combines triple differences with difference-in-discontinuities and organizes wages, mobility, promotion, and firm responses without treating one estimator as universal.
transfer_limit: Multiple estimators address different comparisons and share policy-specific assumptions; their number is not cumulative proof of identification.

title: The Loan Covenant Channel: How Bank Health Transmits to the Real Economy
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Assigns nonparametric, regression, and IV designs distinct jobs; proceeds from loan adjustments to substitution, real effects, aggregate implications, and placebo tests.
transfer_limit: The designs and aggregate exercise rely on special supervisory and covenant data; not every paper needs this many evidence layers.

title: Less Mainstream Credit, More Payday Borrowing? Evidence from Debt Collection Restrictions
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: States the debt-collection policy comparison, reports mainstream and payday credit margins in order, and attaches robustness checks to border and legislation threats.
transfer_limit: Border and policy timing comparisons remain exposed to local concurrent changes; many robustness tables cannot establish one mechanism.

title: Moral Hazard versus Liquidity in Household Bankruptcy
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses separate RKD and IV variation to distinguish generosity-driven moral hazard from payment-driven liquidity, with interpretation adjacent to each design.
transfer_limit: RKD and IV recover different local objects; their estimates should not be blended into a single population-wide causal effect.

title: FinTech Credit and Entrepreneurial Growth
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Makes the approval cutoff intuitive, validates the discontinuity, benchmarks firm outcomes, and divides mechanisms into information and competing cost channels.
transfer_limit: The credit-score cutoff yields a local approval effect and platform-specific information; it is not evidence for all FinTech borrowers.

title: Goal Setting and Saving in the FinTech Era
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Combines beta-tester evidence, matched DiD, parallel-trend assessment, placebo tests, survey evidence, and administrative outcomes to narrow behavioral explanations.
transfer_limit: Beta access, matching, and DiD are not equally strong sources of variation, and post hoc target heterogeneity is not a mechanism by itself.

title: Due Diligence
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Explains selection into due diligence through moments, estimation, bidder heterogeneity, and model-based interpretation; useful for causal-selection writing at the reduced-form boundary.
transfer_limit: Structural selection results depend on maintained bidder and information assumptions; this is not a generic reduced-form causal template.

title: What Is the Cost of Privatization for Workers?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses stacked DiD to place worker losses and productivity benefits in one policy chain, followed by alternative definitions, drivers, heterogeneity, and external validity.
transfer_limit: The benefit-cost comparison is not a full welfare calculation; privatization timing and worker coverage limit transportability.

title: Sending Out an SMS: Automatic Enrollment Experiments for Overdraft Alerts
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Separates experimental design, enrollment effects, charge outcomes, substitution across alerts, and prespecified heterogeneity in an automatic-enrollment setting.
transfer_limit: Alert substitution and automatic enrollment are product-specific; heterogeneous treatment effects do not establish why every user responds.

title: Potential Pilot Problems: Treatment Spillovers in Financial Regulatory Experiments
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Defines direct and indirect treatment effects before estimating them, making interference a central estimand issue instead of a late robustness footnote.
transfer_limit: The paper is a warning about interference; estimates from partial regulatory pilots cannot be read as conventional no-spillover treatment effects.

title: Medicaid and household savings behavior: New evidence from tax refunds
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Places the eligibility instrument next to the savings question and follows the average effect with robustness, financial-hardship heterogeneity, and a constrained-liquidity channel.
transfer_limit: Eligibility and refund timing define the instrument and population; the financial-constraint evidence is supportive rather than formal mediation.

title: CEOs’ Outside Opportunities and Relative Performance Evaluation: Evidence from a Natural Experiment
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses a natural experiment to separate outside opportunities from standard pay-performance stories, then places the principal alternative explanation in its own test block.
transfer_limit: The outside-opportunity shock is context-specific and alternative RPE tests do not make executive-pay mechanisms universally causal.

title: The role of high-skilled foreign labor in startup performance: Evidence from two natural experiments
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Gives two natural experiments nonredundant roles, reports intent-to-treat estimates explicitly, and separates falsification, robustness, and external validity.
transfer_limit: The two shocks identify related but not identical populations and effects; triangulation does not justify pooling their estimates.

title: Color and credit
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses within-market matching, nationwide comparisons, applications, and originations as layered evidence while reporting economic significance and measurement alternatives.
transfer_limit: Matching only balances observables and complaint measures are imperfect; racial disparity evidence requires careful causal and normative wording.

title: On the direct and indirect real effects of credit supply shocks
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Builds and validates a bank-specific credit-supply shock before estimating direct, network, price, and general-equilibrium effects; threats appear before outcome interpretation.
transfer_limit: Shock construction and equilibrium decompositions rely on comprehensive firm-bank and network data; channels are not mutually exclusive.

title: Local banks, credit supply, and house prices
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Leads with an IV specification, then uses DiD and additional outcomes as validation rather than presenting many specifications as interchangeable.
transfer_limit: Local-bank exposure and housing markets may not transport elsewhere; the alternative DiD does not erase IV exclusion concerns.

title: How much should we trust staggered difference-in-differences estimates?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; method; simulations; recommendations; conclusion
teaching_function: Explains why static and dynamic staggered-DiD coefficients can fail, compares alternative estimators, and ends with practical recommendations rather than a table catalogue.
transfer_limit: This is a methods paper and not a license to choose an estimator mechanically; design timing and estimand still govern the choice.

title: Revealing corruption: Firm and worker level evidence from Brazil
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Moves from audit assignment and identification to firm growth, procurement, workers, indirect effects, and competing mechanisms in a disciplined causal sequence.
transfer_limit: Audit exposure and corruption institutions are specific; firm and worker effects do not automatically identify organizational mechanisms.

title: The effects of disclosure and enforcement on payday lending in Texas
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Separates disclosure from enforcement interventions and reports lender and borrower responses without collapsing heterogeneous ordinances into one treatment story.
transfer_limit: Disclosure and enforcement vary across ordinances, so a single pooled label can conceal treatment heterogeneity and implementation differences.

title: Regulatory costs of being public: Evidence from bunching estimation
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Introduces bunching intuition before estimation, documents manipulation, varies counterfactual distributions and windows, and limits cost interpretation to the threshold setting.
transfer_limit: Bunching estimates require a credible counterfactual density and behavioral interpretation; threshold avoidance is not standard RDD evidence.

title: How does competition affect retail banking? Quasi-experimental evidence from bank mergers
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Makes the intervention, DiD comparison, assumptions, first market-structure effect, product outcomes, placebos, and local scope visible in separate steps.
transfer_limit: The effect is local to merger-review intervention and particular banking products; do not infer total consumer welfare from observed prices and quantities.

title: Financial inclusion, economic development, and inequality: Evidence from Brazil
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Moves from a banking-access reform to inclusion, development, inequality, and aggregate outcomes, then uses distance and consumption-versus-business tests to narrow mechanisms.
transfer_limit: The reform changes several margins and aggregate extrapolation needs extra assumptions; distance patterns do not prove one mechanism.

title: The effect of female leadership on contracting from Capitol Hill to Main Street
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Pairs a close-election RDD with validity, placebo, and supply- versus demand-side mechanism sections, making local scope and timing inspectable.
transfer_limit: Close-election RDD estimates are local and political leadership can affect multiple contracting margins; mechanisms remain conditional.

title: Trust as an entry barrier: Evidence from FinTech adoption
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Organizes a scandal-based DiD around trust identification, parallel trends, spillovers, falsification, FinTech adoption, and bounded heterogeneity.
transfer_limit: A scandal may have correlated spillovers and FinTech adoption is context-specific; machine-learned heterogeneity is not mechanism proof.

title: Robust difference-in-differences analysis when there is a term structure
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; method; examples; diagnostics; conclusion
teaching_function: Demonstrates how a term structure can create false or garbled DiD effects, contrasts estimation strategies, and generalizes the diagnostic beyond one application.
transfer_limit: The term-structure pathology is important but not present in every DiD; its remedy must match the data-generating process.

title: Credit supply and house prices: Evidence from mortgage market segmentation
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses mortgage-market segmentation to connect financing choices, quantities, prices, falsification tests, and economic magnitude without overclaiming the population.
transfer_limit: Segmentation-based estimates rely on market boundaries and borrower sorting assumptions; falsifications do not make the effect nationally representative.

title: Price regulation in two-sided markets: Empirical evidence from debit cards
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Writes a two-sided regulation paper by tracking effects on banks, merchants, payment use, and retail prices, then confines interpretation to observed margins.
transfer_limit: Observed bank, merchant, and consumer margins are not a complete welfare calculation, and Durbin regulation is institution-specific.

title: Household mobility and mortgage rate lock
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Explains mobility under mortgage-rate lock with an empirical hazard design, selection-aware comparisons, robustness tests, and an explicit discussion of scope.
transfer_limit: The mortgage-rate-lock effect depends on household selection and rate environments; hazard estimates need not identify every mobility channel.

title: The SOFR discount
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses a benchmark transition and temporary reprieve to sequence secondary-market evidence, alternative specifications, liquidity explanations, and a restrained conclusion.
transfer_limit: The reprieve and benchmark transition are singular events; liquidity evidence can narrow but not uniquely establish the pricing channel.

title: Financial Literacy Externalities
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Separates correlated peer exposure from imitation, education, mobility, and local-labor-market accounts, showing how mechanism alternatives can structure a peer-effects paper.
transfer_limit: Peer exposure can reflect correlated environments and mobility; the alternative tests narrow rather than eliminate every peer-effect confound.

title: Do Neighborhoods Affect the Credit Market Decisions of Low-Income Borrowers? Evidence from the Moving to Opportunity Experiment
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Defines treatment arms and the causal neighborhood object, links random assignment to long-run credit records, and separates credit-demand, credit-supply, and income channels.
transfer_limit: Random assignment identifies neighborhood offers and treatment arms, not every downstream channel; compliance and long-run scope remain explicit.

title: Side Effects of Nudging: Evidence from a Randomized Intervention in the Credit Card Market
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; experimental design; intended/unintended results; discussion
teaching_function: Makes intended and unintended effects equally visible in a randomized nudge and connects attention and psychology evidence to the observed overdraft response.
transfer_limit: The treatment is a specific credit-card reminder; unintended effects should not be generalized to all nudges or all borrowers.

title: What If Dividends Were Tax-Exempt? Evidence from a Natural Experiment
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses a tax exemption as a natural experiment and reports payout, prices, investment, equity, and cash in an order that exposes which margins adjust.
transfer_limit: The tax experiment and payout institutions are special; effects across corporate margins need not imply a complete welfare conclusion.

title: Does Career Risk Deter Potential Entrepreneurs?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Makes the cutoff intuitive, audits validity, and uses explicit rule-out and rule-in tests to distinguish direct career risk from an indirect mechanism.
transfer_limit: The RDD is local to the career-risk cutoff and the direct-mechanism evidence remains tied to that institutional margin.

title: Capital Spillover, House Prices, and Consumer Spending: Quasi-Experimental Evidence from House Purchase Restrictions
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Starts with quasi-experimental house-purchase restrictions, then combines DiD, survey evidence, alternatives, marginal propensity benchmarks, and external-validity limits.
transfer_limit: Housing restrictions generate complex spillovers and survey evidence adds assumptions; the reported MPC is not universally transportable.

title: Credit Building or Credit Crumbling? A Credit Builder Loan’s Effects on Consumer Behavior and Market Efficiency in the United States
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Reports experimental average effects before heterogeneous effects and market-efficiency implications, with an explicit external-validity question.
transfer_limit: The intervention and participants are selected; average and heterogeneous effects do not automatically generalize to the broader credit market.

title: Financial Crises and the Transmission of Monetary Policy to Consumer Credit Markets
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Begins from theoretically ambiguous transmission, then lets 2SLS, identification discussion, placebos, alternative sensitivities, mechanisms, and external validity resolve it.
transfer_limit: The lender and crisis setting constrain external validity; placebo and channel tests cannot prove a unique monetary-transmission mechanism.

title: Deposit Insurance and Depositor Behavior: Evidence from Colombia
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Combines observed bunching with DiD and keeps mechanisms and alternative explanations together, so depositor behavior is tied closely to insurance thresholds.
transfer_limit: Bunching can reflect several motives and the DiD comparison carries timing assumptions; insurance thresholds are institution-specific.

title: Estimating General Equilibrium Spillovers of Large-Scale Shocks
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; estimand framework; bias diagnostics; application; conclusion
teaching_function: Defines direct and spillover estimands, identifies nonlinear and mismeasurement biases, and shows how to diagnose them before making equilibrium or policy claims.
transfer_limit: This is a spillover-method template, not evidence that every estimated indirect effect is general equilibrium or policy relevant.

title: Digital Payments and Consumption: Evidence from the 2016 Demonetization in India
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Compresses shock, first stage, magnitude, persistence, and scope, then assigns tests to purchase substitution, income shocks, credit supply, and the exclusion restriction.
transfer_limit: Demonetization is an unusual shock, and the exclusion restriction plus purchase-substitution tests remain design-specific.

title: Managing Mental Accounts: Payment Cards and Consumption Expenditures
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Triangulates staggered DiD, regression discontinuity in time, and standard DiD, with alternative groups and explanations attached to named threats.
transfer_limit: RDiT and staggered DiD have distinct timing assumptions; agreement across them is not automatic proof against all concurrent shocks.

title: Digitalization and Retirement Contribution Behavior: Evidence from Administrative Data
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Gives rollout-based quasi-experimental and randomized evidence distinct jobs, then links both to retirement contributions and a bounded mechanism discussion.
transfer_limit: Rollout and experiment identify different margins; their convergence does not make digitalization effects universal.

title: Proxy Advisory Firms and Corporate Shareholder Engagement
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Pairs a governance discontinuity with design, placebo, engagement outcomes, and follow-on tests rather than treating the threshold as self-validating.
transfer_limit: The governance cutoff yields a local comparison and proxy-advisor engagement may have multiple pathways; placebos are diagnostic only.

title: The Impact of Crisis-Period Interest Rate Declines on Distressed Borrowers
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Places the mortgage-rate instrument, identification robustness, falsification, borrower outcomes, and welfare interpretation in a transparent evidentiary sequence.
transfer_limit: The instrument and crisis-period rate movements are setting-specific; welfare calculations require assumptions beyond the reduced form.

title: How Does Removing the Tax Benefits of Debt Affect Firms? Evidence from the 2017 U.S. Tax Reform
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Keeps manipulation, predetermined characteristics, magnitude, robustness, falsification, and a DiD alternative around one threshold-based tax estimand.
transfer_limit: The RDD estimate is local to the tax threshold, and the long conclusion should not be imitated as a generic section target.

title: Finance, Advertising, and Race
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses deregulation-based DiD to connect advertising, deposits, racial targeting, language measures, and a persuasion mechanism while preserving interpretive caution.
transfer_limit: Deregulation, advertising language, and racial targeting may share concurrent changes; persuasion evidence narrows rather than proves the mechanism.

title: Effects of Credit Expansions on Stock Market Booms and Busts
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Combines a discontinuity with panel estimates to move from credit expansion to boom-and-bust dynamics and separates implementation from reduced-form evidence.
transfer_limit: Discontinuity and panel specifications identify different margins; boom-and-bust dynamics should not be generalized beyond the credit expansion.

title: The Financial Consequences of Pretrial Detention
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Makes judge-based IV validity, household spillovers, financial outcomes, and bail-related mechanisms separate, auditable elements of the argument.
transfer_limit: Judge assignment supports a local IV object, while within-household spillovers complicate unit-of-treatment and welfare interpretation.

title: The Role of Intermediaries in Selection Markets: Evidence from Mortgage Lending
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; design; validation/robustness; mechanisms/boundaries; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses two-stage selection correction to distinguish intermediary choice from pricing and benchmarks results against a model that ignores endogenous channel selection.
transfer_limit: Selection correction depends on exclusion and functional-form assumptions; intermediary effects are not model-free causal estimates.
